set.st: 29 Aug 1913: two men allegedly robbed the Great Western station at St. Charles of a $1,000 express package. Caught with $100 in half-dollars, they were believed to have buried the other ~$900, all in silver, somewhere between St. Charles and Dover. A Wells Fargo sack of about 72 lb of mixed coin was taken from the locked station by skeleton key. The two young suspects were caught hiding behind trees in a hog pasture on a farm between Dover and Eyota, each with $50 in half-dollars; the rest was thought 'planted' along the way, though the paper also suggested two accomplices may have carried off the bulk. Residents searched the underbrush, ravines and woods along the escape trail; no recovery was reported. Private land: permission. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.pl: St. Charles-Dover-Eyota route along the Great Western line (pin midway between St. Charles and Dover); capture farm between Dover and Eyota not yet placed
set.t: Silver half-dollars respond well to a detector. Accomplices may have taken the bulk. Placing the capture farm between Dover and Eyota would anchor the route's end. Private land: permission.
